Commentary.Commentary: ... RUN CHASE ...

The bowling started on a waivered note and leaked towards both sides of the ground but they held on well in the middle phase and pulled things back in their favor. Vishwa Lahiru, Supun Waduge and Malsha Tharupathi took a couple each while the fielding yielded a couple as well in the form of run-outs. The target doesn't look that big but the Lankan batting has been off-color for the majority of the tournament and that makes this a good contest of cricket. Run chase to begin in a while.

After being put in to bat first, South Africa Under-19 were off to flying colors as the opening pair added 63 for the first wicket ut lost their way in the middle as the wickets kepts tumbling. The young Protea batters did get starts but threw away their wickets. It was then for the 7th wicket partnership of 49 between Romashan Pillay and Riley Norton that helped the host nation score in excess of 200. Riley Norton played a handy innings of 41 runs while Romashan Pillay batted well too for his 27. It was their keeper Lhuan-dre Pretorius who top-scored for the side with 71 runs.
A solid partnership at the top helps South Africa Under-19 to post 232 on board. They now need to defend this and strengthen their chances to qualify for the semis.

Hello and a very warm welcome folks. It is match time for group 2 in the Super Six stage of the ICC Under-19 World Cup. In this match, South Africa Under-19 will clash against Sri Lanka Under-19 at Senwes Park, Potchefstroom. South Africa Under-19 have done well so far in this tournament, They have kept up their consistency and have only lost against the team from England. Their batting unit looks to be in great touch and Lhuan-dre Pretorius has a fine half-century under his belt as well. Their bowling unit also performed exceptionally well and gave the batters a low target to chase down. Kwena Maphaka will be very confident after clinching a fifer in the previous game. This team has momentum in their favor and will want to test their might against the young Lankans. Sri Lanka Under-19 are on a comeback story here. After two consecutive losses, they got a win under their belt in their last game where they played against their counterparts from Zimbabwe. Their top batting order looked out of touch which will be something they will look to improve but their middle order stepped up to the occasion and put some runs on the board. Their bowlers also took responsibility and made sure that the opposition was always under pressure. Malsha Tharupathi was the star with his four-wicket haul. They now have the challenge to beat South Africa Under-19 in this game and it will be great for their confidence if they beat them on their home ground. This is expected to be a thrilling encounter. Toss and team news to follow.
... MATCH DAY ...

With a position in the semi-final up at stake Sri Lanka Under-19 takes on the host nation South Africa Under-19 in game no. 9 of the Super Six stage at the Diamond Oval, Kimberley. Both sides carried a couple of points from their respective group-stage games to Super Six. The hosts Proteas have lost just one game so far and that was a rain-captailed game against England Under-19. The young Proteas have bulldozed past their opponents off late with victories against Scotland Under-19 and Zimbabwe Under-19 in one-sided affairs. The dynamic duo of Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Steve Stolk right at the top has been firing on all cylinders. Steve Stolk in particular is going through a purple patch of his own. Stolk has been well complimented by Dewan Marais who has scored 187 in his last 3 innings with the bat and has been in an eye-catching form. The side is well equipped with powerful strikers along with those who could play the perfect anchor to their partner. The bowling unit looks solid as well with Kwena Maphaka leading the bowling attack along with Riley Norton and Tristan Luus. The young Proteas look en route to the semis with a far superior NRR over their rivals for that last spot from their Super Six group. A defeat wouldn't be all lost for them but a convincing victory could put them on top as well. Sri Lanka Under-19 just like their opponents for the day carried a couple of points as well from their group but they lost to West Indies Under-19 and the chances of them advancing to the semis look slim as they would need to play out of their skin to defeat a strong opponent like South Africa Under-19 and that too in a convincing manner. Cricket surely is a game of unpredictability but for something like this to happen would require a lot of good fortune to bless Sri Lanka Under-19. It is the Lankan bowlers that have kept them alive till this point as the batters have failed to live up to the expectations. Dinura Kalupahana has been the only one putting up some strong batting performances throughout while the others have faltered in each game. The side needs the batters to raise their hand and play for the badge, taking responsibility and helping the side crack a tough nut in South Africa Under-19. Will the Proteas take a giant leap in the race to qualify for the semis or will Sri Lanka Under-19 keep them at bay and produce the upset of the tournament? We shall find out when these sides collide.
